reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a highly structured, quasi-periodic pattern dominated by sharp, narrow downward spikes (troughs) followed by flat or slowly rising plateaus. The fundamental cadence is approximately 1 cycle per ~25–30 points in the robust-standardized space, though exact spacing varies slightly across candidates. Spikes are near-vertical, symmetric or slightly asymmetric, with durations of 1–3 points and depths ranging from ~0.4 to >8 standardized units—indicating amplitude scaling across segments rather than intrinsic shape change. Between spikes, the signal remains stable at a constant baseline (median ≈ 0), with negligible roughness (MAD ≈ 0) and near-zero curvature. A weak linear trend is present globally (slope ~−9e−5), but locally, baselines are flat; candidate 3 shows an accelerated upward ramp late in its window, likely reflecting the global trend amplified over longer duration (427 pts, 5 cycles). Noise is virtually absent: all candidates show near-perfect step-like transitions and zero intra-plateau variation. Acceptable variation includes: (1) spike depth scaling (e.g., 0.5 vs 8.3), (2) plateau length variability, (3) occasional double/triple closely spaced spikes, and (4) minor slope during long windows due to trend. Crucially, the *morphology* of individual spikes—sharp onset, brief trough, rapid recovery—is invariant across reliable candidates.

The late surge reflects accumulation of the global linear trend over extended duration; spike morphology remains consistent. Amplitude scaling is extreme but structurally coherent.
